description: Full 3D vector/analytic-geometry drill set: building vectors AB/AC/BC/OA from point coordinates, vector magnitude, dot product (from coordinates and from magnitude+angle), finding a parameter m for orthogonality, cross product (component form and magnitude), scalar triple product identities, collinearity/coplanarity checks for 3-4 points, triangle area via cross product, parametric/symmetric line equations through two points or point+direction, plane equations (point+normal, point+direction-pair, through 3 points), sphere equations (center+point, diameter endpoints, general-form center/radius), point-to-plane distance, and a large curated bank of real BAC II exam problems (2002-2023) combining all of the above into multi-part questions.

source.description: Cambodian BAC II grade-12 math exercise compendium (Start Up Community), Lesson 12: វិចទ័រក្នុងលំហ (Vectors in Space) — exercises only, no worked solutions
source.extracted_by: manual OCR/transcription from scanned textbook (Claude Code), 2026-08-29

exercises.technique: Build vector components from point coordinates: \overrightarrow{AB}=(x_B-x_A,y_B-y_A,z_B-z_A)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Compute }\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC}\text{ for: }A(1,-2,3),B(2,4,3),C(2,3,5);\ A(2,3,5),B(-5,2,4),C(-1,-3,3);\ A(1,2,4),B(10,2,10),C(5,-1,4);\ \overrightarrow{AB}=\vec\imath+3\vec\jmath-\vec k,\ \overrightarrow{AC}=5\vec\imath-5\vec\jmath+3\vec k;\ \overrightarrow{AB}=2\vec\imath-3\vec\jmath+2\vec k,\ \overrightarrow{AC}(3,5,2);\ \overrightarrow{AB}=2\vec\imath-2\vec\jmath+\vec k,\ \overrightarrow{AC}(5,4,2);\ \overrightarrow{AB}=-\vec\imath+\vec\jmath+\vec k,\ \overrightarrow{CA}=-5\vec\imath+\vec\jmath-\vec k;\ \overrightarrow{BA}=\vec\imath+2\vec\jmath-3\vec k,\ \overrightarrow{CA}=10\vec\imath+3\vec k;\ \overrightarrow{BA}=-5\vec\imath-3\vec\jmath,\ \overrightarrow{CA}=3\vec\jmath+\vec k
exercises.technique: Dot product from coordinates \vec u\cdot\vec v=u_1v_1+u_2v_2+u_3v_3

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Compute }\vec u\cdot\vec v\text{ given }|\vec u|,|\vec v|,\theta: |\vec u|=2,|\vec v|=1,\theta=30^\circ;\ |\vec u|=1,|\vec v|=2,\theta=45^\circ;\ |\vec u|=2,|\vec v|=4,\theta=30^\circ;\ |\vec u|=2,|\vec v|=2,\theta=30^\circ;\ |\vec u|=1,|\vec v|=2,\theta=45^\circ;\ |\vec u|=5,|\vec v|=3,\theta=45^\circ;\ |\vec u|=5,|\vec v|=10,\theta=60^\circ;\ |\vec u|=10,|\vec v|=2,\theta=60^\circ
exercises.technique: Dot product formula \vec u\cdot\vec v=|\vec u||\vec v|\cos\theta

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find }m\text{ s.t. }\vec u\cdot\vec v=0: \vec u=(m,-1,2),\vec v=(1,3,2);\ \vec u=(2,m,1),\vec v=(3,2,m);\ \vec u=(5m,4,3),\vec v=(m,4,-3);\ \vec u=(10,5,-m),\vec v=(1,2,m);\ \vec u=(3,6,m),\vec v=(5,3,5);\ \vec u=(m,3m,10),\vec v=(4,2,-10);\ \vec u=3\vec\imath+m\vec\jmath-\vec k,\vec v=3m\vec\imath-3\vec\jmath+3\vec k;\ \vec u=20m\vec\imath-3\vec\jmath+\vec k,\vec v=10m\vec\imath+20\vec k
exercises.technique: Solve \vec u\cdot\vec v=0 as a linear or quadratic equation in the unknown parameter m

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Compute }\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\text{ and }\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{BC}\text{ for 6 point-triples }A,B,C;\ \text{compute }\vec u\times\vec v\text{ and }|\vec u\times\vec v|\text{ for 8 vector pairs (coordinate or }\vec\imath,\vec\jmath,\vec k\text{ form)}
exercises.technique: Cross product component formula \vec u\times\vec v=(u_2v_3-u_3v_2,\,u_3v_1-u_1v_3,\,u_1v_2-u_2v_1) and its magnitude

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Given }\vec u=(1,2,3),\vec v=(3,1,2),\vec w=(3,4,5): \text{compute }|\vec u|,|\vec v|,|\vec w|;\ \vec u\cdot\vec v,\vec u\cdot\vec w,\vec v\cdot\vec w;\ \vec u\times\vec v,\vec v\times\vec w,\vec u\times\vec w;\ \vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w),\vec v\cdot(\vec u\times\vec w),\vec w\cdot(\vec u\times\vec v);\ \text{Given }\vec u=(1,2,4),\vec v=(1,0,4),\vec w=(-2,3,5): \text{prove }\vec u\times\vec v=-(\vec v\times\vec u);\ \vec u\times(\vec v+\vec w)=\vec u\times\vec v+\vec u\times\vec w;\ \vec u\cdot(\vec v\times\vec w)=(\vec u\times\vec v)\cdot\vec w;\ \vec u\times\vec u=\vec0
exercises.technique: Verify general vector-algebra identities (anticommutativity, distributivity, scalar triple product cyclic property) using specific numeric vectors
Combine magnitude, dot product, and cross product computations for one triangle's vertices

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find scalar triple product }k\text{ of }\overrightarrow{AB},\overrightarrow{AC}\text{ for 3 point-triples}A,B,C;\ \text{check collinearity of }A,B,C\text{ (not on same line, unbiased test) for 4 point-triples}
exercises.technique: Scalar triple product for collinearity/coplanarity testing

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find area of triangle }ABC\text{ using cross product for 6 point-triples;}\ \text{find perimeter/type of triangle }ABC\text{ for 6 point-triples (incl. one given as }\overrightarrow{AB},\overrightarrow{AC}\text{ directly);}\ \text{check coplanarity for 6 vector-triples }\vec u,\vec v,\vec w;\ \text{verify 4 given points }A,B,C,D\text{ form a parallelogram for 3 point-quadruples}
exercises.technique: Triangle area via \tfrac12|\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}|, coplanarity via scalar triple product =0, parallelogram check via \overrightarrow{AB}=\overrightarrow{DC}

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find parametric/symmetric line }(D)\text{ equations: through 2 points (4 items), through a point with a given direction vector (3 items);}\ \text{find line }(L)\text{ equations through a point parallel to another given line, in various forms (symmetric, offset-symmetric, parametric) (9 items);}\ \text{find plane equations through a point with a given normal vector }\vec n\text{ (5 items)}
exercises.technique: Standard 3D line forms: two-point form, point+direction (parametric x=x_0+at, y=y_0+bt, z=z_0+ct, or symmetric (x-x_0)/a=(y-y_0)/b=(z-z_0)/c); plane point-normal form a(x-x_0)+b(y-y_0)+c(z-z_0)=0

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find plane through 3 non-collinear points for 6 point-triples;}\ \text{find plane through a point and the projection plane }yoz\text{ (1 item), }xoz\text{ (1 item)}
exercises.technique: Plane equation via normal \vec n=\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}, or coordinate-plane-parallel plane equations

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find symmetric line equation through a point parallel to the plane's normal, for 6 point+plane pairs;}\ \text{find sphere }(S)\text{ equation: with center }I\text{ through a point (2 items), with diameter endpoints }[AB]\text{ (3 items)}
exercises.technique: Line parallel to a plane's normal vector; sphere equation (x-a)^2+(y-b)^2+(z-c)^2=r^2 from center+point or from diameter endpoints (center = midpoint, r = half the distance)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Find center }I\text{ and radius }R\text{ of sphere }(S)\text{ given general-form equation, for 6 equations like }x^2+y^2+z^2-4x+4y-4z+4=0;\ \text{find distance from 6 named points to given planes }(\alpha)\text{ (e.g. }A(1,5,-4)\text{ to }3x-y+2z=6\text{)};\ \text{find symmetric line equation through a point parallel to a given parametric line }(D)\text{, for 5 point+line pairs}
exercises.technique: Complete the square to extract center/radius from general sphere equation x^2+y^2+z^2+Dx+Ey+Fz+G=0; point-to-plane distance formula d=|ax_0+by_0+cz_0-d|/\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Curated BAC II exam problems by year (2002-2023), one multi-part problem per year, each combining several of: building vectors from 3-4 given points, checking non-collinearity, computing }\overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC}\text{ as a plane normal, finding a plane/line equation, computing triangle area via cross product, verifying a tetrahedron OABC or parallelogram, sphere equations tangent to a plane, point-to-plane distance and projection, checking a right/isosceles triangle via dot product, and finding intersection points between a line and a plane or sphere.}
exercises.technique: Real exam-style multi-part space-geometry problems requiring 4-6 chained sub-computations per year (2002 through 2023, ~22 problems total)

exercises.prompt_latex: \text{Compute}\ \overrightarrow{AB},\overrightarrow{AC},\overrightarrow{BC}\ \text{for 2 point-triples};\ \text{compute}\ \overrightarrow{MN},\overrightarrow{NP},\overrightarrow{MO}\ \text{for 2 point-triples};\ \text{compute}\ |\overrightarrow{AB}|,|\overrightarrow{AC}|,|\overrightarrow{BC}|\ \text{for 2 point-triples};\ \text{compute}\ AB,AC,BC\ \text{(distance) for 2 point-triples};\ \text{compute}\ \overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AC},\overrightarrow{BC}\cdot\overrightarrow{BD},\overrightarrow{AB}\cdot\overrightarrow{AD}\ \text{for 2 point-quadruples};\ \text{compute}\ \overrightarrow{AB}\times\overrightarrow{AC},\overrightarrow{BC}\times\overrightarrow{BA}\ \text{for 2 point-triples};\ \text{compute area of triangle}\ ABC\ \text{for 2 point-triples};\ \text{prove}\ A,B,C\ \text{not collinear for 2 point-triples};\ \text{prove}\ M,N,P\ \text{coplanar with a given line for 1 setup};\ \text{find symmetric-form equation of line}\ (D)\ \text{through a point with given direction vector, for 3 point+vector pairs};\ \text{find equation of plane}\ (P)\ \text{through a point with given normal vector, for 2 point+normal pairs};\ \text{prove 4 points form a trapezoid/parallelogram, for 2 point-quadruples};\ \text{prove 4 points form a rectangle/right-angle figure, for 2 point-quadruples};\ \text{prove triangle right-angled at a vertex for 4 point-triples};\ \text{(BacII2018) given}\ A(1,2,3),B(3,0,1),C(-1,0,1),D(2,1,2):\ \text{compute}\ \overrightarrow{AB},\overrightarrow{AC},\overrightarrow{AD},\overrightarrow{BC};\ \text{prove}\ A,B,C\ \text{not collinear};\ \text{prove}\ \vec n=(0,1,-1)\ \text{normal to plane}(ABC);\ \text{(BacII2019) given}\ A(1,-1,4),B(7,-1,-2),C(1,5,-2):\ \text{compute}\ \overrightarrow{AB},\overrightarrow{AC},\overrightarrow{BC};\ \text{prove}\ A,B,C\ \text{not collinear};\ \text{prove}\ \vec n=(1,1,1)\ \text{normal to plane}\ ABC;\ \text{find plane equation}\ ABC;\ \text{prove triangle}\ ABC\ \text{right-angled}
exercises.technique: Semester-2 review bank (section V): comprehensive vector-in-space review covering all techniques above, plus 2 curated real BAC II exam problems (2018, 2019)
